# Progression Schemes for PeakWeek — The Definitive Report

**Scope:** Linear critique · Wave loading · DUP/undulating · Hypertrophy off-season, for the PeakWeek macOS coaching app (`/Users/richardholguin/dev/powerlifting-trainer`).
**Ground rules honored throughout:** every table below is expressible with the existing `Slot` model (`sets: Int`, `reps: Int`, `pct: Double?`, `rpe: Double`, pool + exercise reference) as generated by `Engine.dayTemplates` (`Sources/PeakWeek/Engine.swift`). Nothing here modifies a factory number — acc 4×6 @ 67–75, trans 4×4 @ 77–86, real 87–93 singles/doubles, deload 62%, meet 60/55%, RTS RPE table, attempts 91/97/101.5, last heavy DL 10–14 d, openers 7–10 d. All schemes are **opt-in per-phase progression schemes** per the composability principle in `docs/roadmap-training-options.md` ("per-phase schemes, not monolithic program types"). Variation loads keep the existing semantics: `load = comp 1RM × pct × mod`, so all % values below are on the **competition** 1RM and the exercise modifier scales them automatically.

RPE calibration throughout uses the engine's own Tuchscherer table (`Engine.rpeTable`): e.g. 5 reps RPE 7 = 79%, 4 reps RPE 8 = 84%, 3 reps RPE 8 = 86%, 2 reps RPE 7 = 86%, 8 reps RPE 7 = 71%, 10 reps RPE 7 = 65%.

---

## 1. Linear progression: honest critique

The factory engine is a **linear intra-block ramp**: each block interpolates `lerp(startPct, endPct, t)` where `t = weekInBlock / (blockLen − 1)`, at fixed sets and reps (e.g. transmutation squat: 4×4 climbing 77 → 86%).

### 1.1 What linear ramps do well

1. **Predictable, auditable overload.** One variable moves. The coach can read week 6 off the plan in January. This matters enormously for a delivery-first tool — the PDF the client receives is self-explaining ("loads rise week to week — trust the percentages," as `weekToText` already says).
2. **Maps directly onto peaking.** A monotonic intensity ramp into a taper is exactly the shape the taper/peaking literature validates (step/exponential taper studies, `docs/research-science.md` §4). Linear realization is close to unimprovable.
3. **Novice/early-intermediate fit.** When week-over-week adaptation genuinely outpaces fatigue, a straight ramp harvests it with zero decision overhead. Meta-analytically, **undulating shows an advantage over linear only in *trained* lifters, and mainly on bench** — in untrained lifters there is no detectable difference ([SBS periodization review](https://www.strongerbyscience.com/periodization-data/)).
4. **Attempt projection.** A known terminal intensity (86% fours → 93% singles → 91/97/101.5 attempts) makes the whole chain — training max → openers — one arithmetic pipeline. That calibration is the engine's crown jewel (spec §A4: "best-calibrated default in the engine").
5. **Low monitoring cost.** No logging or readiness data required — which is honest about what the app can see today (logging is P1).

### 1.2 Where linear fails

1. **Monotony / accommodation.** The same 4×6 or 4×4 for 5–6 straight weeks narrows the stimulus. The app's own science audit calls the static rep scheme out explicitly: *"6 reps flat for 5–6 weeks is monotonous and leaves the hypertrophy stimulus narrow"* (`research-science.md` §8.2). Variation of the rep/intensity stimulus is one of the few periodization mechanisms with a plausible causal story (novel stimulus, motor-pattern breadth, psychological freshness).
2. **Fatigue masking fitness.** The fitness–fatigue model's core claim: expressed performance = fitness − fatigue. A monotonic ramp accumulates fatigue monotonically, so the lifter is *weakest-feeling* exactly when the percentages are highest. Weeks 5–6 of a linear block routinely feel harder than the RPE column promises; nothing in a pure %-ramp releases fatigue until the block ends. Wave loading (§2) exists precisely to periodically unload within the block.
3. **The % is anchored to a stale number.** `pct × comp 1RM` assumes the 1RM is both accurate and constant. Over a 6-week block the true max drifts up (or down); daily readiness varies ±3–5%. Fixed % prescriptions are systematically wrong on both the best and worst days — the entire rationale for RPE capping (Helms et al. 2018 found RPE-based load assignment gave a small probable advantage over %1RM in a DUP program; `research-science.md` §5).
4. **Junk-volume entry weeks.** The audit's cross-check against the engine's own RPE table: 6 @ 67% is below RPE 4 for a trained lifter — a warm-up, not a stimulus (§8.2). Linear interpolation from a too-low floor wastes the first 1–2 weeks of every accumulation block. (Factory numbers stay; the corrected 72–80 preset is already specced as opt-in.)
5. **No volume progression.** Linear-% with fixed sets means the engine progresses *only* load. The audit calls this "the largest single programming gap" (§8.2). Wave/DUP/hypertrophy schemes below all bake in a volume dimension.
6. **Non-responders.** Group-mean equivalence hides individual divergence. Some lifters stall or regress on any fixed ramp; the professional practice answer (Emerging Strategies, `research-practice.md`) is to treat the block as a hypothesis and vary the *scheme*, not just the numbers, for non-responders. A linear-only engine gives the coach no lever except editing cells by hand.
7. **The evidence, honestly.** Head-to-head meta-analyses find **no significant difference between linear and undulating periodization for strength** ([Harries et al. 2015, JSCR](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/25353077/) — 17 studies) **or hypertrophy** ([Grgic et al. 2017, PeerJ](https://peerj.com/articles/3695/)). Block vs DUP in trained athletes: trends favor block, not significant ([Painter et al. 2012](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/22173008/)). The one directional finding: **undulating outperforms linear in trained lifters for bench press but not squat** ([SBS synthesis](https://www.strongerbyscience.com/periodization-data/)). Conclusion for app copy: linear is not wrong, alternatives are not upgrades — they are equal-citizen tools whose value is fit-to-lifter, exactly as `roadmap-training-options.md` frames it ("present as equal-citizen option, not upgrade").

### 1.3 Coach intake questions — "is linear right for this lifter/block?"

Frame these as the questions the app (or the coach's own judgment) should answer before picking a scheme:

1. **Training age?** < ~2 y serious training → linear; the undulating advantage only appears in trained lifters.
2. **Did the last linear block deliver?** e1RM up, RPEs on-script → do not switch. Stalled twice on the same scheme → vary it.
3. **How stale is the entered 1RM?** Tested > 8–10 weeks ago or post-layoff → linear %s inherit the error; prefer RPE-capped or wave (which revisits lighter weeks where miscalibration is cheap).
4. **How variable is the lifter's week-to-week readiness** (shift work, sleep, life stress)? High variance punishes fixed monotonic %s; waves and RPE caps absorb it.
5. **Does the lifter psychologically need variety?** Boredom/monotony is a real adherence variable; DUP's biggest practical win is freshness.
6. **How close is the meet?** Realization: always linear/monotonic into the taper. Transmutation: linear or wave. Accumulation/off-season: the strongest case for undulation and volume ramps.
7. **Does week 5–6 of their linear blocks historically collapse** (RPE blowouts, technique decay)? That is fatigue-masking-fitness — the specific problem waves solve.
8. **Bench-centric goals?** The one lift with meta-analytic support for undulation at higher frequency (3×/wk, per Grgic frequency work and METD 2-3-1 pattern).
9. **Can the lifter execute RPE honestly?** If not (novice guard, spec §A6), prefer pure % linear or wave — both are RPE-independent.

## 2. Wave loading

### 2.1 Canonical structures

A **wave** is a short (usually 3-week) micro-ramp of rising intensity/falling reps, followed by a *drop-back* that starts the next wave slightly heavier than the last one started. The canonical strength-block wave (the coach's own example in `roadmap-training-options.md`):

> Week 1: 4×6 @ 70 → Week 2: 4×5 @ 75 → Week 3: 4×4 @ 80, then repeat **+2.5%** (72.5/77.5/82.5).

Other canonical shapes:

| Pattern | Structure | Typical use |
|---|---|---|
| **3-week volume wave** | 4×6@70 / 4×5@75 / 4×4@80, +2.5%/wave | Late accumulation → strength block |
| **3-week strength wave** | 4×5@79 / 4×4@82.5 / 4×3@86, +2.5%/wave | Transmutation (this app's use case, §2.4) |
| **3:1 step-load** (Stone/Plisk) | 3 rising weeks + 1 unload week (~−1 wave) | Classic "summated microcycle" ([Plisk & Stone, Periodization Strategies](https://www.researchgate.net/publication/245765378_Periodization_Strategies)) |
| **Westside pendulum / DE waves** | 3-week bar-speed waves 50–55–60% (+bands), reset | Conjugate DE work — already noted for the future conjugate build ([Westside, Wave Periodization](https://www.westside-barbell.com/blogs/the-blog/wave-periodization)) |
| **Intra-session waves** (Poliquin-style) | e.g. 3/2/1 @ rising %, repeated ~2–3× in one session, second wave heavier via PAP | Peaking sessions; NOT recommended as a block scheme here — needs multiple slots of 1 set each, clutters the Slot model |

An undulating set-rep-% reference table (strength emphasis, % of comp 1RM), the kind coaches carry in their heads:

| Wave step | Reps | % band | Engine-RPE at top |
|---|---|---|---|
| Step 1 (re-entry) | 5–6 | 70–79 | 5 @ 79 ≈ RPE 7 |
| Step 2 (build) | 4–5 | 75–83 | 4 @ 82.5 ≈ RPE 7.5 |
| Step 3 (peak) | 3–4 | 80–86 | 3 @ 86 ≈ RPE 8 |
| Next wave | repeat | +2.5% each step | +~0.5 RPE |

### 2.2 Why waves manage fatigue

- **Fitness–fatigue arithmetic:** the drop-back week sheds accumulated fatigue while fitness (which decays slower) is retained, so each wave's step 3 is performed at a *better* fitness−fatigue balance than a monotonic ramp would allow at the same calendar week. The wave is a built-in mini-deload every third week without stopping progress — the same logic as the 3:1 step-loading paradigm, where volume/intensity rises for three microcycles and fatigue is deliberately released before it inhibits performance ([SimpliFaster](https://simplifaster.com/articles/rediscover-wave-loading-program-design-for-speed-and-power/), [Plisk & Stone](https://www.researchgate.net/publication/245765378_Periodization_Strategies)).
- **Rep-bracket rotation** keeps three adjacent motor tasks (5s/4s/3s) warm simultaneously instead of grinding one; re-entry weeks double as technique consolidation at loads where miscalibration is cheap.
- **Psychology:** every third week is a visible "win" week; every fourth is visibly lighter. Adherence and bar-speed quality both benefit; sets stay submaximal so per-session strain is capped.
- **Evidence, honestly:** there are no direct RCTs isolating "wave vs straight ramp" at matched volume/intensity in powerlifters. The support is (a) the general step-loading/planned-variation literature (Stone, Plisk, Issurin), (b) the meta-analytic equivalence of undulating and linear (so waves cost nothing), and (c) near-universal practitioner adoption in intermediate/advanced strength blocks. App copy should say "fatigue-management structure with strong practitioner consensus," not "proven superior."

### 2.3 Design of the PeakWeek transmutation wave (rules)

Anchors chosen so the wave **starts and ends where the factory band does** (factory trans squat: 4×4 @ 77 → 86):

- **Wave shape (3 steps, 4 sets throughout):** reps 5 → 4 → 3; the *final* wave for squat is **79 / 82.5 / 86** — peak pinned to the factory ceiling 86%. Engine-RPE check: 5@79 = RPE 7 · 4@82.5 ≈ RPE 7.5 · 3@86 = RPE 8. A clean 7 → 7.5 → 8 ascent.
- **Bench main** is offset −1 (factory bench band 76–85): final wave **78 / 81.5 / 85**.
- **Deadlift main** (factory 4×3 @ 78–87): reps 4 → 3 → 2, final wave **80 / 83.5 / 87** — peak pinned to factory ceiling 87%.
- **Inter-wave increment:** each earlier wave is −2.5% at every step (the coach's own +2.5% reset rule, run backward from the pinned final wave).
- **Remainder rule (N not divisible by 3):** waves = ⌈N/3⌉; drop the first (lightest) `3·waves − N` steps of wave 1. The block therefore always *ends* on the full top wave at 86/85/87, and off-cycle lengths open mid-wave at RPE ≤ 7.
- **RPE caps** (Slot.rpe): SQ/BP step 1 = 7.0, step 2 = 7.5, step 3 = 8.0. DL = 8.0 flat (factory value).
- **Secondary lifts stay on the factory linear lerp** — the wave replaces `lerp(t)` only for the three comp-lift primary slots; pause squat (2×3 @ 70→76), Spoto (3×4 @ 70→76), block pull (2×3 @ 72→78), close-grip Day-4 (4×5 @ 70→76) and five-day pause squat (3×5 @ 68→74) are byte-identical to factory. This is the minimal, composable diff the roadmap asks for ("replaces the lerp(start,end,t) with a wave function over weekInBlock").
- **Rounding note:** the current template helper rounds pct to integers (`pct.map { $0.rounded() }`). `Slot.pct` is a Double and `weekToText` prints halves correctly, so the wave scheme should bypass that rounding; if integer rounding is kept, half-values round half-away-from-zero (82.5→83, 83.5→84, 76.5→77) and the scheme survives intact.
- **Deload interaction:** none. Waves self-unload every 3rd-week drop-back; the factory n≥12 deload insertion and the manual insert-deload feature behave unchanged.

## 3. DUP / undulating for the app's 4- and 5-day splits

### 3.1 How daily undulation is actually implemented when each lift has 1–2 slots/week

Textbook DUP (Rhea, Zourdos) trains the *same lift* 3×/week in three zones — hypertrophy (H), power (P), strength (S). The app's split is lift-per-day (S / B / D / B2 (/ S2)), so honest implementation is a hybrid of three mechanisms:

1. **Across-week undulation (true DUP)** for lifts with 2 slots: bench (Day 2 + Day 4) and, in the 5-day, squat (Day 1 + Day 5) get different zones on their two days.
2. **Within-day undulation** — the main slot and the variation slot on one day take different zones (e.g. comp deadlift S + Romanian deadlift H on Day 3). This is how a 1-slot lift still sees two stimuli weekly.
3. **Week-to-week (weekly undulating) rotation** for 1-slot lifts: the slot's zone alternates by week parity (squat Day 1 in the 4-day alternates H/S). `dayTemplates` already receives week context, so parity-dependent slots are directly implementable.

**Zone order matters:** Zourdos showed hypertrophy → power → strength (HPS) beat hypertrophy → strength → power in competitive powerlifters (greater squat/bench volume and greater bench 1RM gains) ([Zourdos et al. 2016, JSCR](https://journals.lww.com/nsca-jscr/fulltext/2016/03000/modified_daily_undulating_periodization_model.24.aspx)). The templates below order each lift's weekly exposures H → P → S.

**Zone definitions** (accumulation-appropriate; consistent with the coach's roadmap numbers "hypertrophy ~4×8 @ 65-72, power ~6×3 @ 75-82, strength ~3×5 @ 80-87", tuned to the engine RPE table and kept inside accumulation intensity):

| Zone | Scheme | Band over block | RPE cap | Engine-RPE check |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| H (hypertrophy) | 4×8 | 65 → 71% | 7.0 | 8 @ 71 = RPE 7 |
| P (power / speed) | 4×3 | 68 → 72% | 6.5 | 3 @ 72 ≪ RPE 6 — bar-speed work by design |
| S (strength) | 4×5 | 75 → 81% | 7.5 | 5 @ 81 = RPE 8 |
| S-DL | 4×4 | 76 → 82% | 7.5 | 4 @ 82 ≈ RPE 7.4 (DL runs lower RPE at equal %) |

| DB Shoulder Press | 3×12 RPE 8 | | | | | |

Weekly zone map, 5-day: **Squat = H (D1) → P (D1) → S (D5)**, **Bench = H (D2) → P (D4) → S (D4)** — both fully HPS-ordered; DL as in 4-day.

### 3.4 Week-to-week progression rule (any N) and options

- **Percent progression:** every %-bearing slot lerps its band over the block: `pct(w) = lerp(low, high, (w−1)/(N−1))` — the exact factory mechanism, new band constants only. The N = 6 numbers above are those lerps (engine-rounded). Alternating slots evaluate the lerp at their own weeks.
- **Optional volume ramp (recommended toggle, off by default):** H slots run sets 3→4→4→5→5→5 across a 6-week block (RP summated-microcycle pattern, `research-science.md` §2.3) instead of flat 4. Fixes the "no volume progression" gap while remaining pure `sets: Int` data.
- **Optional RPE-led variant:** hold each zone's % at its midpoint and progress the RPE cap +0.5/2 weeks — supported by Helms et al. 2018 (small probable advantage to RPE-based loading in a DUP program); gate behind the novice guard (spec §A6).
- **Deloads:** unchanged factory policy (auto n≥12, manual insertion feature).
- **Evidence framing for the UI:** "comparable to linear in trials; advantage cases are trained lifters and bench" — never "better" ([Harries 2015](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/25353077/), [Grgic 2017](https://peerj.com/articles/3695/), [Zourdos 2016](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/26332783/), [Painter 2012](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/22173008/)).

## 4. Hypertrophy off-season (volume-first, 8–12 weeks, no meet)

**Design intent** (matches `roadmap-training-options.md` §4): main-lift **variations** (not comp lifts) at 8–12 reps @ 60–72% of comp 1RM (the load modifier scales each variation's absolute weight automatically), **accessory volume doubled** vs the factory accumulation day (factory: 2 accessory slots × 3 sets ≈ 6 sets/day; here: 4 accessory slots × 3–4 sets ≈ 12–14 sets/day), deload every ~5th week (aligns with the 4–6-week deload consensus in `research-science.md` §3 and practitioner off-season guides: [JTS](https://www.jtsstrength.com/periodization-powerlifting-definitive-guide/), [PowerliftingTechnique](https://powerliftingtechnique.com/off-season-powerlifting-program/)). Ships as a new `StartPhase.hypertrophy` (decode-safe additive rawValue).

### 4.1 Mesocycle progression spine (main variation slots)

Rep target drops per meso (double progression across mesos), % climbs within each meso, deload = **the factory deload week template, unchanged** (3×5 @ 62 comp lifts + light accessories — reuse `dayTemplates(.deload)`, zero new numbers):

**12-week layout**

| Weeks | Main-variation scheme | % by week | Engine-RPE arc |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1–4 (meso 1) | 4×12 | 60 / 61 / 62 / 63 | ~6.5 → 8 |
| 5 | Factory deload week | 62 (factory) | — |
| 6–9 (meso 2) | 4×10 | 64 / 65 / 67 / 68 | ~6.5 → 8 |
| 10 | Factory deload week | 62 (factory) | — |
| 11–12 (meso 3) | 4×8 | 70 / 72 | ~7 → 7.5 |

**10-week layout:** weeks 1–4 = meso 1 · week 5 = deload · weeks 6–9 = meso 2 · week 10 = bridge week 4×8 @ 70 (hand-off into the next strength block).
**8-week layout:** weeks 1–4 = meso 1 · week 5 = deload · weeks 6–8 = meso 2 compressed (4×10 @ 65 / 67 / 68).
**9/11-week rule:** extend meso 2 (9, 11) by one week inserting 66 (i.e. 64/65/66/67/68); 11-week keeps the week-10 deload and one meso-3 week @ 71.

**Secondary variation slots:** 3×8 fixed, at **main-variation % − 2** each week. **Accessories:** double progression to the top of the listed rep target under the RPE cap, then +1 set on the first two accessories of each day in weeks 3–4 of each meso (3→4 sets); reset after deload.

### 4.2 EXACT 4-day day templates (exercise pool references are the factory library seeds)

Notation: main = the meso scheme above; 2° = main% − 2.

**Day 1 — Squat (quad bias)**
1. High-Bar Squat (mod 0.92) — **main variation** (4×12/10/8 @ spine %)
2. Pause Squat (mod 0.90) — 2°: 3×8 @ main − 2
3. Leg Press — 3→4×12 RPE 8
4. Walking Lunge — 3→4×12 RPE 8
5. Leg Extension — 3×15 RPE 8.5
6. Lying Leg Curl — 3×12 RPE 8

**Day 2 — Bench (chest/triceps)**
1. Close-Grip Bench (mod 0.92) — **main variation**
2. Incline Bench (mod 0.85) — 2°: 3×8 @ main − 2
3. Dip — 3→4×10 RPE 8
4. DB Shoulder Press — 3→4×12 RPE 8
5. Tricep Pushdown — 3×15 RPE 8.5
6. Lat Pulldown — 3×12 RPE 8

**Day 3 — Deadlift (hinge/back)**
1. Romanian Deadlift (mod 0.75) — **main variation** (the 0.75 mod keeps 12s @ 60% of comp max sane)
2. Snatch-Grip Deadlift (mod 0.80) — 2°: 3×8 @ main − 2
3. Barbell Row — 3→4×10 RPE 8
4. Glute-Ham Raise — 3→4×10 RPE 8
5. Seated Cable Row — 3×12 RPE 8
6. Back Extension — 3×12 RPE 8

**Day 4 — Bench 2 / upper volume**
1. Larsen Press (mod 0.90) — **main variation**
2. Feet-Up Bench (mod 0.92) — 2°: 3×8 @ main − 2
3. Pull-Up — 3→4×8 RPE 8
4. Chest-Supported Row — 3×12 RPE 8
5. Overhead Press — 3×10 RPE 7.5
6. Skull Crusher — 3×12 RPE 8

### 4.3 5-day version — adds Day 5, other days unchanged

**Day 5 — Squat 2 & weak points**
1. Safety Bar Squat (mod 0.87) — **main variation** (same meso spine)
2. Box Squat (mod 0.92) — 2°: 3×8 @ main − 2
3. Bulgarian Split Squat — 3→4×10 RPE 8
4. Hip Thrust — 3×10 RPE 8
5. Good Morning — 3×10 RPE 7.5
6. JM Press — 3×12 RPE 8

Fully-worked main-variation numbers, 12-week 4-day (identical spine on D1/D2/D3/D4 mains; 2° in parentheses): wk1 4×12 @ 60 (58) · wk2 4×12 @ 61 (59) · wk3 4×12 @ 62 (60) · wk4 4×12 @ 63 (61) · wk5 factory deload · wk6 4×10 @ 64 (62) · wk7 4×10 @ 65 (63) · wk8 4×10 @ 67 (65) · wk9 4×10 @ 68 (66) · wk10 factory deload · wk11 4×8 @ 70 (68) · wk12 4×8 @ 72 (70).

**Guard rails for copy:** 12s above ~63% or 10s above ~68% blow past RPE 8 on the engine's own table — the bands are deliberately capped; comp-lift skill is maintained by the close variations (pause, close-grip, high-bar), and the first post-off-season block should re-test or re-estimate the 1RM before %-based strength work resumes (reference-max discipline, spec §A4/§8.5).

## 5. Implementation cross-check (why every table above is safe)

- **Slot compatibility:** every prescription is `sets:Int × reps:Int` with either `pct:Double` (halves at most) + `rpe` cap, or `pct:nil` + RPE-only — no AMRAPs, no "work up to," no cluster notation. Conjugate (which does need new prescription forms) is correctly deferred per the roadmap.
- **Generation:** wave = replace `lerp` with a wave function over `weekInBlock` for 3 slots (roadmap item 2); DUP = a parallel `dayTemplates` set with parity-aware slots (item 1); hypertrophy = new `StartPhase` + allocation like `allocateOffSeason` with deload weeks pinned at 5/10 (item 4). All opt-in via the per-phase scheme selector; factory golden tests untouched; each scheme gets its own absolute pins (wave: {79/82.5/86, 78/81.5/85, 80/83.5/87, −2.5 offsets}; DUP: zone bands {65–71, 68–72, 75–81, 76–82}; hypertrophy: meso spine {60–63, 64–68, 70–72, −2 secondary}).
- **Untouched factory surface:** block allocation, deload 62%, meet week 60/55, realization 87–93, attempts 91/97/101.5, RPE table, last-heavy DL timing, opener timing, all secondary/accessory numbers in the wave scheme, and the deload template reused verbatim by the hypertrophy off-season.
